html:
Spanish Guinea was Spain's colony in the Gulf of Guinea, made up of the island of Fernando Po (now Bioko) and the mainland strip of Rio Muni, from 1778 to 1968. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900. It became independent as Equatorial Guinea.

Portugal handed the area to Spain by treaty in 1778, but Spain did little with it for decades. From 1827 to the 1840s the British used Fernando Po as a base for ships hunting slave traders. Spanish settlement picked up later in the 1800s, and the mainland borders with French Gabon and German Kamerun were fixed in 1900.

Fernando Po became a land of cocoa plantations, worked by contract labourers brought from Liberia and later Nigeria under harsh conditions. Independence in 1968 was followed by the brutal rule of Francisco Macias Nguema.
